Definition: Exempting your own case from a standard you apply to others, without justification for the exception. If the standard binds others, the exception needs its own reason.
Example: Someone argues, 'Everyone should cite sources — except me, because I am an expert.'
FaithDiscussionExample: Someone argues, 'Every claim needs reasons — except my favorite preacher's, because he is anointed.'
HowToRespond: Ask for the justification: 'If the standard applies to others, what justifies the exception here?'
